![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226336/assets/34e3bbdee3f70fe0111574f0d0fab772acf98de668e2eeb72464e6611a1fabcd.png)

The area of one loop of the polar curve $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta )$ (shown above) is given by the integral

$$
A=2{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}{cos}^{2}⁡(3\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Which of the following represents the total area bounded by the polar curve?
question.worked_solution:
The given polar curve is the polar rose with $3$ petals, and we know that the area of the first petal is

$$
A=2{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}{cos}^{2}⁡(3\theta )\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226336/assets/34e3bbdee3f70fe0111574f0d0fab772acf98de668e2eeb72464e6611a1fabcd.png)

The $1$st petal is traversed from ${\theta }_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{6}$ to ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{\pi }{6},$ and the length of this interval is $\frac{\pi }{3}.$

To find the interval for the second petal, we have to add $\frac{\pi }{3}$ to both ends of the interval of the first petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{3} & ={\theta }_{1}+\frac{\pi }{3}=-\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{\pi }{6} \\ {\theta }_{4} & ={\theta }_{2}+\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to obtain the interval for the third petal, we add $\frac{\pi }{3}$ to both ends of the interval of the second petal:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{5} & ={\theta }_{3}+\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{\pi }{2} \\ {\theta }_{6} & ={\theta }_{4}+\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{5\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, we obtain the following intervals for all $3$ petals of our rose:

$$
{{[-\frac{\pi }{6},\frac{\pi }{6}]}_{⏟}}_{1\text{st}},\,{{[\frac{\pi }{6},\frac{\pi }{2}]}_{⏟}}_{2\text{nd}},\,{{[\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{5\pi }{6}]}_{⏟}}_{3\text{rd}}
$$

Therefore, the total area of the given polar curve can be obtained if the curve is traversed from $\theta =-\frac{\pi }{6}$ to $\theta =\frac{5\pi }{6}:$

$$
{A}_{\text{total}}=2{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{5\pi /6}{cos}^{2}⁡(3\theta )\,\text{d}\theta 
$$
